remit: underpriced hawkish policy, higher terminal rates, or higher-rate repricing
stance_summary: US inflation persistence and a still-firm demand/labor mix are not consistent with a finished-enough hiking cycle. Verified: Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16-Sep, official SOFR is 3.85% on 17-Sep, SR3U7/SOFR_2027-09 implied 4.755% is the 3m-strip peak (+90.5bp vs overnight) then the strip eases, 6m core PCE is still ~3.0% annualized, U-3 4.1% with NFP +162k and AHE +3.1% y/y, ISM services 55.4 with activity/orders above 60, August retail +1.2% m/m, BoJ hiked to 1.25%, BoE held 3.75% with three hike votes. Inference: the 4.755% peak-then-ease path underprices the reaction function if core stays above target with labor/services still hot. Unknown: CFTC/CME positioning, NZ rates, executable broker quotes. Book action is HOLD of existing short SOFR_2027-09 pos-c9184707c12b; do not OPEN a duplicate.

trade.structure: outright pay / short duration in CME 3m SOFR Sep-2027 (SR3U7), marked in implied-rate space

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: Pay/short SOFR_2027-09 (SR3U7) outright: own the US terminal implied at packet mid 4.755%, the peak of the CME 3m SOFR strip.
expression_comparison.spot_candidate: Long USDCAD as the FX expression of a higher US terminal versus cooler Canadian labor (score 38) and core near 2%.
expression_comparison.rationale: The discrepancy is the US policy-path peak and the small post-peak easing, which SR3U7 owns directly in implied-rate space. USDCAD mixes oil-supply tails (Saudi workaround versus weaker energy shock absorbers), BoC energy pass-through, and CAD-specific labor softness; it is a noisier claim on the same US reaction function. The frozen packet has a complete US SOFR 1m/3m path. Rates is the cleaner expression and is already the open book position.

context_build.causal_mechanism: If US core inflation remains above a 2% policy-neutral pace while labor and services demand stay expansionary, the Fed's reaction function delivers a higher terminal (or delayed easing) than a strip that peaks at 4.755% in Sep-2027 and then eases. Sticky 6m core PCE near 3%, positive payrolls, and hot services orders keep the tightening bias live after the 16-Sep 25bp hike; global policy (BoJ hike, BoE hike minority, energy pass-through) raises the odds that the Sep-2027 peak is not the cycle's last word.
context_build.path_to_current_price: Overnight SOFR was 3.62% on 16-Sep and 3.85% on 17-Sep after the Fed raised 25bp to 3.75-4.00%; futures had entered that meeting with a greater-than-90% probability of the 25bp hike, so the delivered move is largely known. UST 2Y is 4.76% as of 18-Sep, +57bp over 1m and +9bp on 1d, 99.8th 1y percentile; 5Y 4.86% and 10Y 5.01% are likewise 99th-percentile 1y. US 2s10s is 25bp, 0.2nd 1y percentile, flattened 21bp over 1m — a bear-flattening into a priced hiking path. On the tradable 3m SOFR strip, implied rates run 4.00% (Sep-26, +15bp vs overnight), 4.32% (Dec-26, +47bp), 4.58% (Mar-27, +73bp), 4.72% (Jun-27, +87bp), peak 4.755% (Sep-27, +90.5bp), then 4.73% / 4.695% / 4.66% into 2028. The 1m SOFR strip reaches 4.525% by Apr-27 (+67.5bp). Cash 2Y 4.76% matches SR3U7 4.755%, so the sovereign 2Y is the same terminal, not a separate story. Existing paper short SOFR_2027-09 was opened the prior run at that 4.755 mid and is still unmarked versus it.
context_build.known_vs_new_information: Known before this freeze: August CPI kept the Fed tightening bias intact (11-Sep), the 16-Sep 25bp hike was >90% priced, and 6m core PCE ~3.0% / labor 4.1% were already in the gauges. Genuinely newer in the packet: official SOFR printing 3.85% on 17-Sep (the hike in the overnight benchmark), BoJ raising to 1.25% (31-year high), BoE holding 3.75% but splitting 6-3 with three hike votes, energy-market shock absorbers weakening, and the desk thesis that the Fed hawkish turn is now reinforced by broader global tightening. The Saudi-Oman workaround is also new and cuts the extreme oil-supply tail — a partial offset, not a disinflation close. The Sep hike itself is not a reason to add; the reason to stay short the 2027 peak is that the strip still treats the cycle as finished enough by late 2027 despite still-hot US gauges and a live global tightening impulse.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: From 3.85% overnight, the 3m SOFR strip prices about 90.5bp of additional tightening by Sep-2027 (roughly three-and-a-half 25bp steps) and then about 21bp of easing by Jun-2029 (4.545%). Dec-26 3m at 4.32% is only +47bp — barely two additional 25bp hikes through year-end. The priced assumption is a completed-enough hiking cycle with a modest terminal near 4.75% and early, shallow cuts after the 2027 peak.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: The disagreement is not that the Sep hike was missed; it is that 4.755% as the strip peak, followed by easing, is too low and too early if 6m core PCE stays near 3% with U-3 4.1%, payrolls still positive, ISM services 55.4 and orders above 60, and August retail rebounding 1.2%. A reaction function that just hiked on sticky inflation should not already be pricing the last hike into a 2027-09 peak plus cuts. SR3U7 is the contract that owns that peak.
context_build.price_decomposition: Level versus change: overnight 3.85% is the post-hike cash benchmark; the 23bp 16-to-17-Sep SOFR jump is the delivered 25bp feeding into the fixing, not a new terminal. Tenor split: 1m contracts map the near-term path (Oct 3.91% through Apr-27 4.525%); 3m contracts map the terminal (peak SR3U7 4.755%). Marginal driver of the 2Y/SR3U7 complex is the hiking path, not term premium — 2s10s at a 1y extreme of 25bp shows the front end, not the 30Y (5.34%, +15bp 1m), did the selling. Cross-market: CA-US 2Y is -140bp (3.8th 1y percentile) because CORRA prices a larger additional hike cycle (+84bp by Mar-27, +136bp by Jun-28) from a 2.29% overnight despite cooler CA inflation/labor; that is CAD-specific energy pass-through, not evidence that US terminal is already rich. AU 2Y 4.999% is 99th percentile with AONIA still pricing ~60bp of extra tightening, consistent with a global hawkish impulse but with housing transmission already biting.

historical_reference.distribution: UST 2Y 4.76% sits at the 99.8th 1y percentile and 88th 5y percentile; 5Y/10Y are 99th-percentile 1y. US 2s10s 25bp is the 0.2nd 1y percentile after a 21bp 1m flattening. Those extremes are a discovery signal that a large hawkish repricing already happened over the past month (+57bp 2Y); they are not proof the terminal is high enough. The SOFR 3m strip's +90.5bp peak-then-ease shape is the economically relevant distribution for this trade, not the 2Y percentile alone.
analogs: 2022-23 US hiking cycle: markets repeatedly treated a near-term SOFR/FF peak as the terminal and then repriced the peak higher while core inflation stayed above 2% and payrolls stayed positive.
2023 skip-then-resume: a pause was priced as cycle-end and was not; the reaction function stayed data-dependent with inflation still too high.
historical_reference.regime_differences: Overnight is already 3.85% after a delivered 25bp hike, not mid-2022's first hikes from the effective lower bound. 6m core PCE ~3.0% and 1m/3m ~2.4% are sticky-above-target, not 2022 goods-inflation spikes. Energy is an overlay with both weaker shock absorbers and a Saudi workaround that cuts the extreme oil tail. ISM manufacturing 54.6 is still expansionary rather than a deep goods recession. Positioning cannot be compared to 2023 because CFTC/CME positioning is unavailable in this packet.

independent_checks: Policy path: official SOFR 3.85% versus ICE 1m SOFR through Apr-27 (4.525%, +67.5bp) and CME 3m SOFR peaking at SR3U7 4.755% (+90.5bp) then easing — two contract families tell the same 'hike then done' story.

Hard macro gauges: US inflation 72 (Jul core PCE +0.2% m/m, ~2.4% 1m/3m and ~3.0% 6m annualized), labor 75 (U-3 4.1%, AHE +0.3% m/m / +3.1% y/y, NFP +162k with positive revisions), activity 69 (ISM services 55.4 with activity/orders above 60; GDP +1.5% SAAR is the soft leg), consumer 74 (August retail +1.2% after a weak July, against weaker confidence).

Sovereign confirmation: UST 2Y 4.76% as of 18-Sep matches SR3U7 4.755%, so the cash 2Y is not a cheaper or richer terminal than the futures peak; the mispricing is the path shape, not a 2Y-vs-SR3 basis.

Global policy triangulation: BoJ to 1.25%, BoE 6-3 with three hike votes, RBA tightening already visible in NSW stamp duty -24% y/y and Sydney/Melbourne values more than 7% off peak, BoC minutes flagging energy pass-through — the easing impulse is constrained even where domestic growth is softer.

CA: overnight CORRA 2.29%; 3m strip +84bp by Mar-27 (3.13%) and +136bp by Jun-28 (3.65%). AU: overnight AONIA 4.35%; 1m strip to 4.945% by Jul/Aug-27 (+59.5bp). NZ policy path is not in the packet.

trade.thesis: FACT: Fed delivered 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16-Sep; official SOFR is 3.85%; SR3U7 implied 4.755% is the 3m peak then the strip eases; 6m core PCE still ~3.0%; labor and services demand remain firm; BoJ hiked to 1.25% and BoE had three hike votes. INFERENCE: that peak-then-ease shape is a 'cycle finished enough by late 2027' assumption that underprices inflation persistence and the post-hike reaction function. UNKNOWN: spec positioning and NZ rates. Expression: stay short duration / pay SOFR_2027-09 so the mark rising in implied-rate space is the P&L. This is a HOLD of pos-c9184707c12b, not a second OPEN.
trade.mispricing: SR3U7 at 4.755% (+90.5bp vs 3.85% overnight) plus subsequent easing prices a completed-enough US hiking cycle. Sticky 6m core PCE near 3% with labor score 75 and ISM services 55.4 is a higher-terminal or delayed-easing distribution, not a 4.75% peak and cuts.
why_now: Overnight SOFR has printed the hike at 3.85% (17-Sep), but the 3m strip still peaks at 4.755% in Sep-2027 and then eases — the terminal/easing assumption is now cleanly visible against the new cash benchmark.
August CPI kept the Fed tightening bias intact; 6m core PCE ~3.0% and August retail +1.2% keep demand-side inflation risk alive after the meeting.

Desk thesis: the Fed hawkish turn is now reinforced by BoJ 1.25% and a BoE 6-3 split; energy shock absorbers weakening is a second inflation-persistence channel even after the Saudi workaround cuts the extreme oil tail.
Existing short SOFR_2027-09 already owns this peak; the packet has not invalidated it, so the book action is HOLD of pos-c9184707c12b rather than a duplicate OPEN.
